text:
Jacob Trouba won the Messier Leadership Award as the Rangers' captain in 2024, and now he's the veteran voice on a young, losing Sharks team, playing about 22 minutes a night. He has 10 points in 19 games, seven in his last ten, which is more offense than his recent seasons would suggest.

His game is still about the defensive blue line. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows him stopping 16% of the entries aimed at him, against a typical 11%, so opponents dump it in on his side more often. The weakness is the other direction: only 28% of his exits keep possession, and NHL Edge has his top speed near the bottom tenth of the league. Against a heavy forecheck, that shows.

San Jose is better with him than without him, about five points of expected goal share, though the team overall is at 46% with him on. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season, split between Anaheim and the Rangers. Our range has him at 30 to 48 points over a full season. He's the kind of defenseman a contender asks about in February; for now he's the adult in the room.
headline: Trouba, the adult in San Jose's room
